kernel.governing_law: Love among women is a field of fierce possession: intimacy generates hierarchy, betrayal is choosing another circle, and tenderness survives only as the residue of accusation — relation is sustained through its denunciation.
kernel.mutated_relation: The denunciation as the vow itself — every accusation a declaration of binding, every insult the ceremony that consummates the bond it claims to refuse.

independent.recovered_law: Text B systematically inverts the relational valence: hostility, arrogance, complaint, and repulsion in Text A become devotion, binding commitment, loyalty, and intimacy in Text B — antagonistic or distancing relations between persons are replaced by bonding or pledging relations.
independent.law_match_note: Both describe the same structural inversion: hostile/denouncing speech acts become binding/pledging acts — accusations become declarations of commitment, insults become ceremonies of bonding.
independent.terminal_note: The final section (Day and Night 36) maintains the inversion: 'let you' becomes 'lose you,' 'bitch' becomes 'darling,' 'mist of dew' becomes 'breath of one mouth' — the bonding relation holds throughout.
